artworks.title: El amour y la muerte (Love and Death)
artworks.medium: etching, burnished aquatint, and burin on laid paper

artworks.title: Quien lo creyera! (Who Would Have Thought It!)
artworks.medium: etching, burnished aquatint, and burin on laid paper
artworks.description: This is a painting depicting two figures in a struggle with bear-like creatures in a dark environment. The figures seem distressed, and the creatures appear threatening. The shading and lines create a sense of tension, contributing to the overall atmosphere of horror and despair.

artworks.title: A caza de dientes (Out Hunting for Teeth)
artworks.medium: etching, burnished aquatint, and burin on laid paper
artworks.description: The image shows two figures shown from head to toe in a dramatic scene. The figure on the left is a woman standing side by side with a man. She leans slightly backward with her head tilted to her right and one arm raised, while the other hand grasps the man's hands. Her facial features are detailed, with a look of concentration. She has long flowing hair, wears a floor-length dress with intricate patterns, and a garment draped over her shoulders. She stands on a raised platform with her left foot slightly pointed and bent. The second figure, a man, appears pale and mostly wearing a light-colored garment. He hangs limply from a rope just beneath his jaw, with his feet a few inches off the ground. He is barefoot, with dark unkempt hair. The background is a dark, barren landscape, adding a somber tone to the composition.

artworks.title: Asta su abuelo (And So Was His Grandfather)
artworks.medium: lift-ground aquatint and aquatint on laid paper
artworks.description: This print shows an anthropomorphic figure that looks like a donkey sitting upright and wearing the clothes of a human. The donkey sits sideways on a platform, facing the left, with its torso upright and legs balanced on a surface. The donkey has long ears that stand straight up and a snout featuring prominent nostrils and a slight smile. It wears a jacket with a high collar and trousers. The donkey is holding a large open book that rests on the platform in front of it, featuring images of donkeys on each visible page. There appear to be other, indistinct objects around it. The background is gray with a simple speckled pattern.

artworks.title: Ni mas ni menos (Neither More nor Less)
artworks.medium: etching, burnished aquatint, drypoint, and burin on laid paper
artworks.description: The image shows a donkey sitting for a portrait painted by a monkey. In the background, there is an easel with a partially completed donkey's head painting. The donkey sits upright while the monkey paints with a brush and palette.

artworks.title: Linda maestra! (Pretty Teacher!)
artworks.medium: etching, burnished aquatint, and drypoint on laid paper

artworks.title: El sueño de la razon produce monstruos (The Sleep of Reason Produces Monsters)
artworks.medium: etching and aquatint on laid paper
artworks.description: This print shows a man resting his head on his folded arms on top of a desk, which is in the bottom left corner. Under his head, papers rest on the desk next to a few writing implements. The man is dressed in a light-colored garment with loose sleeves and light breeches, and he has short, dark hair. Surrounding him are owls and bats, some resting on him or near him, and some flying in the air above him. A large cat-like animal sits in the bottom right corner, looking towards the man. The background is gray with small white dots, and there are words written in white on the light gray desk.

artworks.title: Si amanece; nos vamos (When Day Breaks We Will Be Off)
artworks.medium: etching, burnished aquatint, and burin on laid paper
artworks.description: This is a painting depicting grotesque figures gathered under a starry night sky. The scene shows a group of bizarre, nude figures with exaggerated and distorted features huddled together on the ground. One figure in the foreground is pointing upwards towards the sky, and the backdrop is a dark night sky filled with stars. The figures have elongated limbs and emaciated bodies, creating an ominous and surreal atmosphere. The style resembles that of Francisco Goya.

artworks.title: No te escaparas (You Will Not Escape)
artworks.medium: etching and burnished aquatint on laid paper

artworks.title: Duendecitos (Hobgoblins)
artworks.medium: etching and burnished aquatint on laid paper

artworks.title: Y son fieras (And They Are Like Wild Beasts)
artworks.medium: etching, burnished aquatint, and drypoint
artworks.description: The image depicts a confrontation scene with several historical figures involved in a dramatic struggle. The monochrome composition intensifies the dramatic effect. Some figures are grounded, while others are in aggressive stances, emphasizing tension. The background is minimal, directing focus to the conflict.

artworks.title: Fuerte cosa es! (That's Tough!)
artworks.medium: etching, burnished aquatint, and drypoint
artworks.description: This is an illustration depicting a scene of violence and drama. A figure with a large sword stands in a menacing pose in the center. To the right, two figures hang from a tree by the neck, with one partially obscured by shadows. On the left, a form on the ground appears to be interacting with the central figure. The landscape is barren and bleak, conveying tension, chaos, and brutality. The figures are detailed with expressive gestures, while the background is sketched more loosely, emphasizing the foreground actions. The drawing uses stark contrasts and dramatic lighting to intensify the emotional impact of the scene.

artworks.title: Por que? (Why?)
artworks.medium: etching, lavis, drypoint, burin, and burnisher
artworks.description: The image depicts three figures in a physical altercation. Each figure wears a uniform and carries a sword. The central figure appears distressed, while the other two are pulling on them. The background is minimally detailed.

artworks.title: Que valor! (What Courage!)
artworks.medium: etching, aquatint, drypoint, engraving, and burnishing
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a cannon and fallen figures. The scene shows a cannon in a barren landscape. The cannon's barrel is central with wheels partly visible. Several figures are seen lying on the ground near the cannon. The art style features strong lines and contrasts, typical of etching techniques, giving a somber and dramatic feel. The composition conveys tension and valor, common in historical or wartime themes.

artworks.title: No se puede saber por que (One Can't Tell Why)
artworks.medium: etching, burnished lavis, drypoint, and burin
artworks.description: The etching features the full upper bodies of five seated men in dark robes and caps, with additional lighter garments draped over their shoulders. Their faces are long and somber, with exaggerated features and dark beards. Each man holds a cross-like object in their folded hands. The background is a simple textured surface, emphasizing the figures. An inscription below the figures reads "No se puede - saber por que."

artworks.title: Ni por esas (Neither Do These)
artworks.medium: etching, lavis, drypoint, and burin
artworks.description: The image depicts multiple figures in a dramatic confrontation. The central figure appears to be engaging with others around them, conveying urgency and struggle. The use of stark contrasts and dark shading enhances the tense atmosphere. A building silhouette is visible to the left, emphasizing the interaction. This painting is in the style of Francisco Goya.

artworks.title: Y no hai remedio (And There's No Help for It)
artworks.medium: etching, drypoint, burin, and burnisher
artworks.description: The image depicts a figure bound to a wooden pole, wearing a blindfold with arms tied behind. There are lifeless bodies on the ground, and a line of soldiers with rifles in the background. The scene is in the style of Francisco Goya.

artworks.title: No se convienen (They Do Not Agree)
artworks.medium: etching, drypoint, burin, and burnisher
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a chaotic battle scene with soldiers engaged in combat. Several soldiers are depicted on foot and horseback, with one rider on horseback raising an arm. Figures are engaged in close combat, wielding swords and other weaponry. The background is filled with smoke or clouds, enhancing the sense of chaos and movement within the scene. The composition is in black and white, with strong contrasts and intricate line work detailing the figures and their surroundings.

artworks.title: Yo lo vi (I Saw It)
artworks.medium: etching, drypoint, and burin
artworks.description: This is a drawing depicting several figures engaged in a dramatic interaction. The foreground shows two figures in motion, with others in the background contributing to the chaotic scene. In the background, a hilly landscape is visible with a mound that could represent a distant fort or castle. The figures appear to be involved in a narrative conveying urgency or tumult. The scene is designed in a monochromatic palette, typical of etchings, emphasizing light and shadow to convey emotion and depth.

artworks.title: Y esto tambien (And This Too)
artworks.medium: etching, aquatint or lavis, drypoint, and burin
artworks.description: The image shows a group of figures walking together carrying large bundles. The figures are moving from right to left, huddled closely together. They appear to be struggling under the weight they are carrying, as large bundles are slung over their shoulders. The figures are depicted in intricate details, with texture and movement in their garments. The background is a mix of dark and light shading, with a gloomy, textured sky. The drawing conveys a mood of hardship and perseverance.

artworks.title: Tanto y mas (Even Worse)
artworks.medium: etching, lavis, and burin
artworks.description: This is a painting of multiple figures lying on the ground in different poses. Their clothing is depicted in dark tones against a light background of an overcast sky and a simple structure in the distance. The scene suggests a moment of aftermath, with figures and objects like swords lying still. The work likely conveys themes of tragedy and conflict. This is done in the style of Francisco Goya.

artworks.title: No se puede mirar (One Can't Look)
artworks.medium: etching, burnished lavis, drypoint, and burin
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a group of people in distress. The scene shows figures in different poses of anguish and despair, depicted in a sketch-like style with strong contrasts between light and shadow. The dark background emphasizes the spotlighting effect on the central figures, creating a dramatic atmosphere. Sharp and ominous surrounding objects hint at a possible threat or danger.

artworks.title: Modo de volar (A Way of Flying)
artworks.medium: etching, aquatint, and drypoint
artworks.description: This drawing depicts various human figures in flight. The main figure is at the center with large, bat-like wings. Surrounding them are several other figures with different styles of wings or flight apparatuses. The background is dark, and the figures stand out against it. The detailed textural lines give a sense of exploration of human flight.

artworks.title: Nada (Nothing)
artworks.medium: etching, aquatint and lavis with burnishing (proof) on laid paper
